subject: POC Trial: Model Selection & Success Criteria
messages:
From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: alice.chen@acmehealth.com, samir.patel@acmehealth.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & next steps from today's discovery — POC scope

Hi Alice / Samir —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed POC plan so we have shared expectations: 

Summary of needs
- Primary use: multilingual clinical note summarization (EN, ES, FR) and entity extraction for billing codes.
- Latency SLO: 200ms p50, 500ms p95 for single-record summarization.
- Throughput expected: ~50 qps during business hours, burst to 200 qps.
- Security: data must stay in customer VPC for production; trial can use dedicated tenant with strict logging.

Proposed POC scope (2 weeks)
- Week 0: Test data ingest & evaluation harness (you'll share 150 sample notes).
- Week 1: Baseline with open model + Redwood serving config; measure latency/cost.
- Week 2: Optimize (quantization, batching, fallback routing) and run evals vs success criteria.

Success criteria (to be validated)
- Summarization ROUGE-L >= 0.48 on your evaluation set OR high qualitative acceptability from 3 clinical reviewers.
- Entity extraction F1 >= 0.85 for billing.Code mapping accuracy >= 80%.
- Performance: p95 latency <= 500ms and mean cost per 1k tokens < target TBD (we'll model after initial run).

Model proposal for trial
- Primary open model: Llama2-13B-instruct-QLoRa (quant-friendly variant) — good balance of cost/quality for English and Spanish with some FR capability.
- Fallback: Mistral-7B-v0 for low-cost, degraded-quality fallback when capacity constrained.
- Multilingual improvement: use small prompt engineering + instruction-tuned adapter; evaluate need for a dedicated FR model after Week 1.

Next steps
1) Send 150 sample notes and a short labeling guide (data shared with Samir).
2) I'll send a POC SOW + evaluation plan and a short onboarding checklist.
3) Kickoff call Tuesday (suggest 10am PT) to confirm infra access and measurement dashboards.

Attaching a one-page SOW and the eval plan template for reference.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

Attachments: RD-2398_POC_SOW.pdf, RD-2398_eval-plan.xlsx

From: alice.chen@acmehealth.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: samir.patel@acmehealth.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps from today's discovery — POC scope

Hey Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. This aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We'll provide 200 pseudo-anonymized notes (mix of EN/ES/FR — ~70/25/5 split). We'll include a short labeling guide and a small gold set (30 notes) with ground truth. Expect to deliver by EOD Friday.
- For success criteria, the product team prefers qualitative acceptability over strict ROUGE for summaries. Can we add a "clinician acceptability >= 80%" checkbox conducted by our clinical reviewers?
- On latency: 200ms p50 is a hard preference; p95 500ms is acceptable as you wrote. If p95 exceeds 800ms, we'll need to discuss fallback routing earlier.
- Security: trial should run in your dedicated tenant with restricted egress; production will require VPC/private deployment. Please confirm data handling.

Model questions:
- We're concerned about FR quality; if Llama2-13B underperforms on FR, we may need a separate FR-specialized model. Can you scope that contingency into the eval plan?

We'll join the Tuesday 10am PT kickoff. Can Marissa be included for operational handoff?

Thanks,
Alice Chen
Head of AI | Acme Health
alice.chen@acmehealth.com

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: alice.chen@acmehealth.com, samir.patel@acmehealth.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps from today's discovery — POC scope

Great — thanks for the quick reply, Alice. Confirming the items and updates: 

- Please send the 200 notes + labeling guide by Friday; we'll ingest into the eval harness and run the gold set.
- We'll add "clinician acceptability >= 80%" as a co-equal success metric (we'll provide a simple rubric for the reviewers).
- Trial infra: we'll spin up a dedicated tenant with restricted egress and detailed audit logs. No data will be used for model training; we'll add that language to the SOW.
- FR contingency: yes — we'll include a fallback plan to evaluate BLOOMZ-7B or a French-tuned variant if Llama2-13B misses the FR threshold after Week 1.

Model selection rationale (short):
- Llama2-13B-instruct-QLoRa: instruction-tuned, strong EN/ES performance, supports quantized inference which helps hit latency/cost targets.
- Fallback Mistral-7B-v0: lower-cost, good inference throughput; expected to degrade summary quality but maintain availability under load.
- FR fallback: BLOOMZ-7B or a small FR-tuned variant depending on initial FR results. We'll run bilingual prompt templates and compare.

Kickoff: Tuesday 10am PT works. Marissa — can you own operational onboarding (infra + dashboards)? Jordan — can you be on the call for model/ops questions?

I attached an updated SOW with the data handling clause and the eval plan with the clinician rubric placeholder.

Cheers,
Ben

Attachments: RD-2398_POC_SOW.pdf, RD-2398_eval-plan.xlsx
